pos.personaBrief: Fluminense keep the ball in tight overloads and want 'to have the ball and make something happen' (Sky Sports), though Diniz admits tiring from possession; the team seeks control, not giving the ball away.

pro.personaBrief: Short build-up from the keeper with deep numerical superiority, even against the press (Football Analyst, Blizzard), with patient short passing and movement after each pass; Diniz mocks the long ball as 'variation'.

est.personaBrief: Position is a function of relationships between players (Hamilton); a-positional 'organised chaos', constant rotation, players clustered around the ball, toco y me voy.

lar.personaBrief: Wingers and full-backs come inside, play tilts to one ball side with triangles, then a switch for a 1v1; the focus is compact proximity play rather than wide stretching.

blo.personaBrief: Aggressive counter-press to win the ball back quickly, squeezing the pitch with a high line; Diniz says the team marked well in high, mid and low lines, but high is the default.

mar.personaBrief: Marking is unresolved in the sources; players hold positions when losing the ball and the team squeezes space and closes the centre, which points to a space-and-ball oriented approach rather than strict following of one man.

pla.personaBrief: Diniz insists on his own model against any opponent, says variation is not dropping the line, and keeps the plan (Trivela: boldness); he shapes it around available players though.

res.personaBrief: Football as art, like painting or music (Diniz 2023); how the team plays matters, and it plays to win away from home without settling, staying bold when ahead.

sis.personaBrief: The collective relationships make technical players shine, while freedom to the technical player and the classic 10 (Ganso) is central; it is not a rigid drilled system.

jog.personaBrief: Technical futsal-inspired football with Ganso as the classic number 10 who links play; technique over physicality.

bas.personaBrief: Fluminense 2023 won with a mix: veterans like Ganso and Marcelo plus young players such as a 20-year-old right winger kept in the XI; youth is trusted but signings matter.

lid.personaBrief: Diniz, a psychology graduate, says the core of his work is good human relations, letting players err without being attacked; he manages people with trust.
